dedupe_keys.name: momepy urban morphometrics in python pysal

description: momepy, short for Morphological Measuring in Python, is a library for quantitative analysis of urban form, part of PySAL and built on GeoPandas, other PySAL modules and networkX. It measures dimensions of morphological elements and aggregates, quantifies shapes, captures the spatial distribution of elements and relations between kinds, and computes further measures listed in its documentation, including street network connectivity. It is described in a Journal of Open Source Software paper (DOI 10.21105/joss.01807) and has tests, coverage reports and a Discord community. Coverage: generic, any city with building and street data. Access: free package, source and documentation. Licence: BSD 3-Clause, copyright Martin Fleischmann and PySAL developers. Caveats: results depend on the quality and consistency of footprint and street data. Simulation uses: describing building and street form for exposure models, urban typology classification and network inputs. Related records: cityseer, the Urban Network Analysis toolbox and PySAL spopt.
